summary: Isle Haute light in the upper Bay of Fundy: a wooden tower lit 1879, burned 1956, replaced by a steel skeletal light. Now a National Wildlife Area; entry needs a permit.

structures.note: 53 ft (16 m) square wooden tower attached to a dwelling; burned October 1956 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Station established 1878 (Rowlett; Conlin via Coleman).
Automated light on a skeletal tower after the fire; square skeleton tower on the Coast Guard list.

access.note: National Wildlife Area: entry prohibited year-round unless authorised by permit (Canada.ca). Rowlett: site and tower closed; visits need Wildlife Service permission. A boat operator at Advocate lists trips to the island (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); Canadian Wildlife Service (site manager)

events.note: Government of Canada appropriated funds for a lighthouse on Isle Haute
Captain Nelson Card appointed keeper 20 Nov 1877 at $500 a year. Contract for the tower ($3,700) awarded to Calvin Cogswell in 1877.
Station established 1878 (Rowlett; Conlin via Coleman). Tower erected under the 1877 contract (LighthouseFriends).
Light first placed in operation 15 Jan 1879 (LighthouseFriends)
George J. Reid keeper from 1889 (LighthouseFriends keeper list)
Percy E. Morris keeper from 1904; the 1909 keeper table gives appointment 2 Aug 1904 at $530 (matched by position)
Fire in October 1956 destroyed the wooden tower and the attached keeper's house
Automated light established on a skeletal tower after the fire; human occupation ended
Designated a National Wildlife Area (gazetted 2025); announced 15 Jan 2025

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station was established in 1878 (Rowlett; Conlin's report as Coleman summarises it), and LighthouseFriends gives 15 January 1879 as the first lighting. The record keeps 1878 as the station year and this file sets first_lit to 1879 from LighthouseFriends. The editor should choose one before publication.

The 1878 wooden tower burned in 1956 and is gone; the steel skeletal tower built after the fire stands today (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett; Coast Guard list). Both statements hold, so the OSM 'standing' record refers to the skeletal tower.

notes_for_editor: Conflicts: keeper's first name (Nelson Card in LighthouseFriends; Leon Card in Conlin's report as Coleman summarises it); station year (1878 for the station per Rowlett and Conlin; 15 January 1879 first lighting per LighthouseFriends). The text gives both. Heights: the Coast Guard list gives the structure 13.0 m; Rowlett gives 12 m (40 ft); the OSM record gives 13.0 m. Both are stated in Today and After the keepers; the sources do not reconcile them. Percy E. Morris's 1904 appointment and $530 salary come from the 1909 keeper table (report of 1909, printed 1910, scan 167, printed 160). Name, date and salary are on one OCR line, but the station is matched by position: the station list and the name list are separate columns. The 1904 start agrees with LighthouseFriends and SaltWire, which supports the match. Coleman's blog and the SaltWire reprint are second-hand: Conlin's 1997 curatorial report (cited by Wikipedia as No. 90, p. 17) was not read. The 1931 article is copyrighted, so only short phrases are quoted in the story. The Snow treasure episode rests on LighthouseFriends alone; the 1952 Life article and Snow's book were not read. The 'about twenty miles' visibility is given as miles, as printed; no nominal range is given. Advocate boat trips (LighthouseFriends) sit alongside the National Wildlife Area entry rule; the operator was not checked. No USLHS roster (US only). The Chronicling America search for 'Isle Haute' returned nothing usable.
